title: random
goal: In this lesson you will learn random for chance events, using seed(1) so practice rolls stay the same.
idea: The random module picks chance values for games. In lessons we call random.seed(1) first so the “random” numbers stay the same every Run — fair for checking answers. random.randint(1, 6) rolls a dice from 1 to 6.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the third roll's print label to Roll 3:. Press Run. Numbers should stay 2, 5, 1 because of the seed.

practice.text: Import random, seed(1), print two dice rolls 1–6.
practice.hint: Fill both empty print() lines with random.randint(1, 6). Keep random.seed(1) so your rolls match the lesson.
practice.starterTip: Try print(random.randint(1, 6)) twice. With seed(1), expect 2 then 5.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if seed(1) and two randint(1,6) prints show 2 then 5.

practice.text: seed(1). Use random.choice on ['a','b','c'] twice and print both.
practice.hint: Make a list like letters = ["a", "b", "c"], then print random.choice(letters) on each blank line.
practice.starterTip: Example: print(random.choice(["a", "b", "c"])) twice. With seed(1), output should be a then c.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if outputs are a then c with seed(1).

quiz.question: Why call random.seed(1) in lessons?

options.text: So rolls match every Run for checking

quiz.correct: A fixed seed makes practice predictable.

quiz.question: Does seed change after you set it once?

options.text: Later randint calls advance the sequence

quiz.correct: The sequence is fixed but not one constant forever.

project.title: Dice Roller
project.desc: seed(1). Print five dice rolls labeled Roll 1..Roll 5.
project.starter:
import random
random.seed(1)
for i in range(1, 6):
    print()
